analysis: The trial executed successfully but achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.4175, below the stated 0.505 reference by 0.0875. Category HR@10 was 0.480 for Movies_and_TV, 0.460 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.350 for Electronics, and 0.380 for CDs_and_Vinyl. These results do not support the proposed candidate-conditioned similarity architecture as an improvement. Possible limitations include weak sequence-order modeling beyond learned recency, compression of history into a weighted embedding sum, and supervision of only one sampled transition per training example. These are hypotheses; the available results do not establish the cause. No training curves or selected epochs were supplied, so convergence and overfitting cannot be assessed. Reported GPU allocation was 521.73 seconds.
code_summary: Trains one independent attentive item-similarity network per category, with separate source/history and target/candidate embeddings. Candidate-conditioned additive attention pools history embeddings using a learned logarithmic recency penalty and history-length normalization. Scores use the pooled-history/target dot product, learned scale, and jointly trained item bias. Training uses random prefixes, 32 sampled negatives excluding training-history items, binary logistic loss, AdamW, dropout, and gradient clipping. Validation selects a single checkpoint per category by HR@10, evaluated every five epochs with early stopping. The generated predictor routes datasets and loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category; no ensembles or separately fitted auxiliary scores are used.
